principle_text: When the persuadee shows emotional concern or curiosity about a serious issue, you should present urgent and impactful information to deepen their engagement and prompt action.
When the persuadee shows confusion or misunderstanding, avoid vague statements that lack clear information or a direct call to action.
When the persuadee expresses curiosity about the legitimacy of the cause, avoid making abrupt direct requests for money without first establishing trust and providing credible information.
When the persuadee explicitly denies shared knowledge, avoid assuming they understand or agree without clarification, as this can cause confusion and reduce engagement.
When the persuadee is unsure about your organization, you should mention a well-known charity to establish common ground and build trust for further engagement.
When the persuadee shows recognition of the charity, you should make a clear, simple donation request to encourage immediate commitment.
When the persuadee has already committed to a donation amount, avoid asking directly for a higher amount without reinforcing their motivation or providing new incentives.
When the persuadee has already committed to a donation amount, avoid asking questions that do not encourage increased commitment or clarify the donation details.
